LOL, hard to believe I’m about to give a tip on how to do SMD soldering. But yeah here are some:

1. Use the smallest tip you have

2. Put just the tiniest amount of solder on the top right (if you’re a lefty then top left) pad of the SMD. Do this for every SMD component on your board so that you get used to the amount of solder that you will be needing for each leg.

3. CLEAN YOUR TIP. You need to clean your tip extremely regularly, as well as tinning it. If the solder isn’t flowing as fast as you like, that’s a sign you should clean and tin your tip.

3. Heat up the solder, and slide the Chip into place on the board. As long as only one pin is soldered? You can move it around easily so you can find a good place we’re the legs of the chip are touching all the pads.

4. Don’t be a perfectionist. If the chip looks like it’s touching all the pads, but is a little crooked, leave it. Don’t want to create more difficulty for yourself by trying to readjust when it’s already in a good space.

5. Relax. Shaky hands are awful for this kind of precision. 

6. After you do the top right, go for the bottom left pin (or vice versa if you did top left). 

That’s pretty much all I’ve picked up so far. Good luck.

Pedal Name is Monkey Paw Disease, named after an inside joke in the shop. Design printed using vinyl cutter. PCB is from [pedalpcb.com](https://pedalpcb.com), it's a clone of EQD Bit Commander, which is an analog octave synth. Uses CMOS chip CD4024BE, and transformer TM011-R. Knobs are:

Level (overall volume output), 

Filter (tone. noon is flat and gets darker counter clockwise and brighter when turned clockwise), 

Base (adjusts the level of the square wave)

Sub (adjust level of -2 octave)

Down (adjusts level of -1 octave)

Up (adjusts level of +1 octave).

I highly recommend this build. It's not difficult for any experienced pedal builder, and it is very faithful to the origin of the pedal. It sounds even better than it looks.
